_provenance.paper: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions (ICLR 2026)
_provenance.note_on_competency_naming: The paper's own four competency names are Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding and Selective Forgetting; its own four published dataset splits are Accurate_Retrieval, Conflict_Resolution, Long_Range_Understanding and Test_Time_Learning. There is no separate Selective_Forgetting split. The Conflict_Resolution split's own task (FactConsolidation: a fact is stated, then restated with a different value later in the same context, and the query asks for the CURRENT value) is the one place in the public data that exercises both named competencies at once: answering it correctly requires resolving which of two conflicting facts is current (conflict resolution) and not answering with the superseded one (selective forgetting). This fixture is built from that split for exactly that reason, stated here rather than left for a reader to reconcile.
_provenance.license: MIT (per the dataset's own HuggingFace listing)
_provenance.row_used: metadata.source == 'factconsolidation_sh_6k' (single-hop, ~6k token context; the smallest of the four single-hop/multi-hop x context-length variants in this split, chosen for a fast deterministic run, not for a better score)
_provenance.extraction_method: This split's context is a numbered list of subject-relation-object fact sentences (e.g. '223. goaltender is associated with the sport of ice hockey.'), where FactConsolidation restates some facts later in the list with a different object (e.g. '310. goaltender is associated with the sport of pesapallo.'), and the paired question ('Which sport is goaltender associated with?') is answered by the LATEST restatement only. For each of the split's 100 (question, answer) pairs: find every fact line ending in the exact answer text, score each candidate's prefix (the line with the trailing answer value removed) against the question's own content words (a small stopword list removed), and accept a candidate only when exactly one has a strictly best score of at least 1 shared content word (otherwise the pair is NO-DATA: no confident single match). Given the accepted prefix, search the same context for any OTHER fact line starting with that exact prefix but ending in a different value; the earliest such line is the superseded fact (NO-DATA when none exists: this row was Accurate Retrieval shaped, not a real conflict). Verified: every mapped item has superseded_position < latest_position (the dataset's own chronological order is preserved, never fabricated), zero duplicate (prefix, latest value) pairs, and unique ids.
_provenance.person_name_filter: This row's own rule is never to print a client name or a person's name other than the founder's. The Wikidata facts behind FactConsolidation are mostly biographical (a real named individual as subject or object: a director, an author, a spouse, a citizen), so of the 74 items the extraction above mapped, every item whose question or fact text names a real person was reviewed by hand and excluded, moved into this fixture's own no_data list with the reason 'excluded: ... names a real person'. What remains is facts about sports, positions, countries, continents, languages, capitals, religions of polities, and companies, none of them a person. This shrinks the mapped set from 74 to 29; it is a deliberate content filter, not an extraction failure, and is called out here rather than folded silently into the same NO-DATA count as the format mismatches.
